items.question: What is the significance of beings being assembled, variegated, and yet similar?
premises: Beings appear assembled together
Beings display variegated forms
Beings also share similarity
items.inference: The coexistence of diversity and similarity among beings calls for a deeper explanation.
items.plain_english: They are assembled, variegated, and yet similar—what indeed is the meaning of this?

items.question: Why do deluded beings fail to recognize Śiva despite his presence?
premises: Śiva remains unknown to fools
They are deceived by Śiva's power
The deception affects those very beings
items.inference: Ignorance of Śiva arises because deluded beings are veiled by his own power.
items.plain_english: But he remains unknown to fools; if they are deceived by Śiva's power, then they alone are the ones deceived.

rows.grounds: the state of being a mine of jewels

items.question: Does the misfortune of the deluded diminish the ocean's nature as a jewel-mine?
premises: The deluded are struck by misfortune
Their misfortune arises from limitation
The ocean remains a mine of jewels
items.inference: The limitation of the unfortunate does not diminish the ocean's inherent richness.
items.plain_english: They alone are struck by misfortune due to their limitation; but is the ocean's nature as a mine of jewels in any way diminished?

items.question: What effort is required for one who delights in the unity of the self?
premises: There is delight in one's own self
This delight arises from unity
Unity leaves no lack to be fulfilled
items.inference: For one established in self-delight through unity, no effort is needed.
items.plain_english: When there is delight in one's own self due to unity, what effort could there be here?

rows.grounds: the discourse on the bliss of delight; also evokes Rāma's bliss
in the experience of that reality

items.question: Why is the discourse on bliss still examined in the experience of reality?
premises: Self-delight is complete in unity
The discourse on bliss is still examined
Examination occurs in the experience of reality
items.inference: Even in complete self-delight, the discourse on bliss is explored within lived experience.
uncertainties: rāmānanda may be read as 'Rāma's bliss' or 'the bliss of delight'
items.plain_english: Even so, the discourse on bliss is indeed examined in the experience of that reality.

items.question: What makes the moon uniquely preeminent among all luminous bodies?
premises: There are many lights
The moon is called the light of lights
The moon alone is the treasury of digits
items.inference: The moon stands uniquely supreme among lights as the repository of all phases.
items.plain_english: Among lights, there is one light indeed—the moon alone, the treasury of digits.

items.question: What establishes the sun as the singular victorious jewel in the sky?
premises: The sun is one and alone
The sun is victorious and renowned
The sun is the jewel of the sky
items.inference: The sun is uniquely preeminent as the renowned and victorious jewel in the heavens.
items.plain_english: One alone is victorious—the sun, who is renowned as the jewel in the sky.

rows.grounds: one whose abode is unknown to jewel-knowers

items.question: Who can truly know the essential nature hidden from expert jewel-knowers?
premises: The abode is unknown to jewel-knowers
Only someone rare may know it
What is known is the true nature
items.inference: The true nature remains inaccessible to experts and is known only by a rare one.
uncertainties: Compound analysis of ratnābhijña+a+vidita+dhiṣaṇaḥ is interpretive
items.plain_english: Someone, whose abode is unknown even to jewel-knowers, knows its true nature.

items.question: Can ordinary knowers fully grasp the value or quality of that supreme nature?
premises: The true nature is rarely known
Value and quality are in question
Ordinary knowledge is implied as limited
items.inference: Ordinary knowers cannot fully comprehend its value or quality.
items.plain_english: Do they truly know its value fully, or its quality?

items.question: What transformative effect does the vision of that reality have on the mind?
premises: One may behold that reality
The mind is likened to an ocean
The vision causes a surging of supreme essence
items.inference: Merely seeing that reality makes the ocean of the mind surge with supreme essence.
items.plain_english: Whoever, merely by seeing it, makes the ocean of the mind surge with supreme essence.

rows.grounds: to the doer who brings about the end of all

items.question: To whom is homage due for the power that brings all things to their end?
premises: There is a power that effects the end of all
Time is the agent of that ending
Homage is offered to that Time
items.inference: Salutation is due to Time, whose power brings about the dissolution of all.
items.plain_english: Salutation to that Time, by whose power the doer brings about the end of all.

rows.grounds: for their own reason or purpose

items.question: Does the disregard of others cause any harm to the supreme reality?
premises: Some disregard that reality for their own reasons
Disregard is an act of the deluded
The reality remains unaffected
items.inference: Though some disregard it for their own reasons, no harm comes to that reality.
items.plain_english: They disregard it for their own reasons, but there is no harm whatsoever to it.

items.question: How should one respond to the full essence regardless of others' attitudes?
premises: The essence is full and complete
One may drink and rejoice in it
Others may blame it without effect
items.inference: One should freely drink and rejoice in the full essence, whether others blame it or not.
items.plain_english: Let one drink the full essence and rejoice, or let one blame it.

items.question: How was the ocean established as a vast repository of jewels?
premises: The ocean was formed with a great belly
This formation occurred at the beginning
It was made a mine of jewels
items.inference: The ocean was fashioned from the outset with vast capacity to be a repository of jewels.
items.plain_english: Having first formed a great belly, the ocean was made a mine of jewels.

rows.grounds: in the state of Sāhib Kaula

items.question: Who is the one delighted in the playful state of Sāhib Kaula?
premises: There is a state called Sāhib Kaula
One is delighted in playful manifestation there
That one is named Śrī Śakti
items.inference: The one named Śrī Śakti is delighted in the playful state of Sāhib Kaula.
uncertainties: anyanu is an unusual form, taken as 'afterwards' per hint
items.plain_english: Afterwards, in the state of Sāhib Kaula, the one named Śrī Śakti delighted in playful manifestation.

items.question: What characterizes the ever-new manifestation abounding in its own essence?
premises: The manifestation abounds in its own essence
It is ever-new
Its freshness arises from its own nature
items.inference: The manifestation is ever-new because it abounds in its own intrinsic essence.
items.plain_english: Abounding in its own essence, it is ever-new.

rows.grounds: by dissolution into one's own mind or view

items.question: How is the ever-new reality perceived by those of ruined or dissolved mind?
premises: Some have a destroyed mind
Some have dissolution into their own view
The reality remains ever-new
items.inference: Whether approached by a ruined mind or by dissolution into one's own view, the reality remains ever-new.
uncertainties: sva+mata+layā could mean dissolution of one's own view or absorption in one's own mind
items.plain_english: Whether by a destroyed mind or by dissolution into one's own view, it remains ever-new.

rows.grounds: endowed with diverse arts or powers

items.question: What is the nature of the power that comprehends Śiva through diverse arts?
premises: It possesses various arts or powers
It comprehends Śiva
Diversity and comprehension coexist
items.inference: The reality endowed with diverse arts fully comprehends Śiva.
items.plain_english: Possessing various arts, it has comprehended Śiva.

rows.grounds: a stream of those who bow down

items.question: What blessing is sought from the stream of those who bow in reverence?
premises: There is a stream of bowing devotees
A blessing is requested
The blessing sought is auspiciousness
items.inference: The stream of reverent bowing is invoked to grant auspiciousness.
items.plain_english: May the stream of those who bow down grant auspiciousness.

rows.grounds: for the waving of lights, for honoring
may it appear or shine forth

items.question: What purpose does this daṇḍaka composition serve in honoring the Goddess?
premises: This is a composition named daṇḍaka
It is offered to Śrī Devī
It is intended as an illumination or honoring
items.inference: This daṇḍaka composition shines forth as an act of illumination in honor of Śrī Devī.
items.plain_english: May this, named a daṇḍaka, shine forth as an illumination for Śrī Devī.
